answer: Forging duplicates costs a fresh credential plus escalating bond slashing, making mass identity farming economically irrational. To resist sybils, each agent must stake a unique proof-of-personhood credential bound to a verified identity before joining the summit of active peers. A pigment-style fingerprint hash of the credential seals it against copying, and a bridge contract cross-checks it against the registry, rejecting any wallet that reuses a credential. Attackers thus pay steep per-identity costs while honest agents pay once. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
